questions.explanation: Caching avoids redundant transfers, gzip/Brotli shrink payloads, pagination limits what is fetched, and connection pooling reuses sockets. Extra threads and longer timeouts move just as many bytes, and dropping TLS is a serious security regression.

questions.question: How would you implement an A/B testing feature-flag system in production?
options: Remote configuration, deterministic user-based variant assignment, per-variant analytics, and percentage-based rollout
Compile two separate apps, each shipping only one variant
Randomly flip features per network request with no stable assignment
Flip the flag for every user at once and watch the crash report after a week
questions.explanation: A/B tests need stable variant assignment, metrics to compare conversions, gradual rollout to limit blast radius, and a kill switch to disable instantly on trouble. Randomized-per-request or global flips destroy experiment validity and safety.

questions.question: Which change gives the largest, safest win for faster incremental builds in a large Android project?
options: Modularize so edits only rebuild affected modules, and enable Gradle build and configuration cache
Disable R8/minification in release builds to speed up compilation
Consolidate everything into one module to avoid inter-module overhead
Buy faster hardware and leave the build configuration untouched
questions.explanation: Modularization plus build/configuration cache attacks the dominant cost - redundant rebuilds. Minify affects release packaging, not incremental dev builds, and performance work should be guided by --profile/Build Analyzer measurements.

questions.question: What does "promotion" mean in the Google Play release flow?
options: Moving the already-uploaded release that passed a lower track up to the next track
Re-uploading the same APK to the production track manually
Rebuilding the app from source before pushing to production
Releasing to 100% of users immediately after the first upload
questions.explanation: Promotion reuses the identical tested artifact - you do not re-upload or rebuild, so what was validated in internal/open testing is exactly what ships. Combined with staged rollout percentages, this limits the blast radius of a bad release.

questions.question: What should you verify before shipping an Android release build?
options: Test the minified release build, check R8 keep rules and mapping.txt, verify android:exported and PendingIntent flags, and test deep links and notifications
Only confirm the project compiles in debug mode
Skip release testing because R8 never changes behavior
Rely on the Play pre-launch report alone without manual testing
questions.explanation: R8 can strip code that works in debug, keep rules and mapping.txt matter for crash reporting, and release gating checks like android:exported and PendingIntent.FLAG_IMMUTABLE are easy to miss. Pre-launch reports complement, but do not replace, testing the actual minified artifact.

questions.question: What is the recommended strategy for migrating a legacy View-based app to Jetpack Compose?
options: Strangler fig: migrate leaf components first, ship new features in Compose, and use AndroidView/ComposeView interop during the transition
Rewrite the entire UI in a single release to avoid a mixed stack
Pause all new feature work until the migration is fully complete
Render the whole app with WebViews while the migration is planned
questions.explanation: Incremental replacement keeps the app shippable throughout. Interop APIs (AndroidView and ComposeView) let View and Compose coexist, and testing at each step catches regressions before the migration finishes.

questions.question: How do you keep state manageable in a complex Compose application?
options: Unidirectional data flow, hoist state to shared owners, use ViewModels as the source of truth, and rememberSaveable for transient UI state
Store all state in a singleton so every screen can read it directly
Keep mutable state inside composable bodies and mutate it in place
Use one global mutableStateOf map updated from anywhere in the app
questions.explanation: Unidirectional flow with hoisting and a single source of truth keeps state predictable; remember covers ephemeral UI state and rememberSaveable survives config changes. Singletons and globals create hidden coupling that is hard to test.

questions.question: What is the most idiomatic way to build a complex custom UI in Compose?
options: Use the Layout composable for custom measurement/placement, Canvas for drawing, Modifiers for behavior, and keep it well tested
Create a custom Android View and host it via AndroidView, isolated from Compose state
Assemble standard components in nested Boxes using fixed pixel offsets
Render a static image of the UI and layer click handlers on top
questions.explanation: Custom Layouts provide tailored measurement and placement, Canvas handles custom drawing, and Modifiers encapsulate behavior. Preferring native Compose building blocks keeps the UI reactive and testable; fixed offsets and static images break under different sizes and languages.

questions.question: Which approach best diagnoses slow startup or scroll jank in Compose?
options: Macrobenchmark for repeatable startup/scroll numbers, plus Perfetto/Systrace traces and Compose Compiler metrics
Open Layout Inspector and infer performance from the hierarchy
Watch the app on a device and guess which function is slow
Check the CPU load of the developer’s host machine
questions.explanation: Macrobenchmark gives stable, reproducible measurements; Perfetto/Systrace identifies the hot frames; and Compose Compiler metrics reveal recomposition and stability problems. Guessing or using host metrics misleads because they do not reflect on-device behavior.

questions.question: When should you use Compose Compiler stability reports?
options: When profiling shows a real stability-driven recomposition problem - the reports are compile-time and identical across debug/release
Always, before any optimization, to fix every unstable class
Only in release builds, because debug builds hide instability
Never, because recomposition order is fully deterministic
questions.explanation: The reports show skippable/restartable status and per-class stability so you can target @Stable/@Immutable fixes precisely. Because the analysis is compile-time, build type does not change the results - and you should optimize only after actually measuring a recomposition issue.

questions.question: What does Strong Skipping mode do in the Compose compiler?
options: Makes all restartable composables skippable and memoizes all lambdas inside composables - enabled by default since Kotlin 2.0.20
Turns off skipping altogether so composition stays deterministic
Requires manual @Stable annotations on every parameter to work
Removes lambdas from the emitted bytecode entirely
questions.explanation: Strong skipping compares unstable parameters by instance equality and auto-memoizes lambdas, so most code gets faster without manual @Stable work; opt out with @NonSkippableComposable or @DontMemoize. Watch for code that relied on side effects in now-skipped lambdas.

questions.question: What is the most effective way to reduce flaky Android UI tests?
options: Deterministic fixtures, test tags/idling resources instead of sleeps, animations disabled, and a quarantine+retry policy
Add longer sleeps before every assertion so the UI always settles
Run the full suite in parallel on many physical devices with no retries
Delete every test that only fails intermittently
questions.explanation: Flakes come from nondeterminism: fixed data, semantic selectors, a controlled test clock, and a quarantine workflow reduce the flake rate while preserving coverage. Sleeps and deletions either mask the real cause or silently remove protection.

questions.question: Which approach most reliably tests coroutine code that switches dispatchers?
options: Inject dispatchers, set Main to a StandardTestDispatcher, drive virtual time with runTest, and assert Flows with Turbine
Use the real Dispatchers.Main and add generous delays until the test passes
Call collect() inside the test and hope the flow completes before timeout
Refactor every function to return synchronously so no coroutines exist
questions.explanation: runTest gives deterministic virtual time, swapping Main keeps the production dispatch order visible, and Turbine asserts emissions without race-sensitive waits. Real-time delays reintroduce the exact flakiness coroutines were meant to remove.

questions.question: What is the most robust way to select a composable inside a Compose UI test?
options: Add a testTag and locate the node with onNodeWithTag, then assert on accessible semantics
Match the node by its exact pixel coordinates on the screen
Assert on the internal composable function name
Dump the rendered bitmap and compare it against a stored image
questions.explanation: Semantics-based selection (testTag/text/role) is independent of layout and pixel positions, so refactors and different screen sizes keep the test valid. Pixel and implementation-based matchers are brittle and fail for no product reason.

questions.question: Which statement best demonstrates that AI improved engineering productivity measurably?
options: Collecting a concrete baseline (e.g. PR review time, defect rate) and comparing it after adoption on the same team with matched control periods
A general sense that the team ships faster since enabling Copilot
The total number of lines of code the AI assistant generated
Comparing two unrelated teams with different workloads and features
questions.explanation: Measurable means a defined baseline, a metric tied to outcomes (not tool usage), the same or matched population, and enough time to separate signal from noise. Tool-generating lines and anecdotes are not causal evidence.

questions.question: Which architecture best supports offline-first sync on Android?
options: Local database as source of truth, an outbox queue for pending writes, WorkManager-driven sync with backoff, and explicit conflict resolution
Cache API responses in memory only and always fetch fresh data in flight
Store all data in RAM and re-download everything on each launch
Block the UI until the network returns so cached state is never shown
questions.explanation: Offline-first needs a durable local store, a durable write queue so user actions are never lost, managed retries with backoff, and explicit conflict policy. In-memory or blocked caches fail the moment the network or process disappears.

questions.question: What makes a media upload pipeline survive process death and flaky networks?
options: A database-backed job driven by WorkManager with exponential backoff, chunked resumable uploads, and idempotency keys
Uploading on the main thread and blocking until the network call finishes
Holding the file only in memory and uploading when a handler fires later
One un-cancelable network request with a very long timeout
questions.explanation: Persistence plus constraint-aware scheduling plus idempotency makes retries safe and resumable across process and network death. Main-thread or in-memory approaches lose state the moment anything interrupts them and can freeze the UI.

questions.question: How should you approach a memory leak that only reproduces occasionally in production?
options: Enable LeakCanary/heap analysis in QA builds, reproduce with a repeatable open-close flow, and inspect the retained chain to find the owner
Increase the app heap size in the manifest so the leak never crashes
Restart the activity automatically whenever memory pressure rises
Ignore Java-side leaks and assume the OS reclaims memory for you
questions.explanation: Leak analysis needs a repeatable repro and the retainer chain to identify the strong reference keeping the object alive. Raising the heap or restarting delays the symptom; the OS never reclaims objects that are strongly reachable.

questions.question: Which combination most reliably reduces cold app startup time?
options: Measure with Macrobenchmark, defer initialization via the App Startup library, ship baseline startup profiles, and theme the window background
Show a blank screen longer so the first frame appears instant by comparison
Preload the entire dependency graph synchronously in Application.onCreate
Disable the launcher animation and ship without measuring
questions.explanation: Startup work should be measured and then removed from the critical path: lazily initialized providers, precompiled startup profiles, and a non-blank first frame. Blocking init and empty screens either slow the real cold start or hide it rather than improve it.
